evidence_type: first-party disclosure: SEC 8-K exhibit press release naming this as Tron Inc.'s own designated on-chain TRX treasury wallet, with a TronScan link provided by the filer itself for live tracking
notes: Scope: narrowly supports only that Tron Inc. (Nasdaq: TRON), a publicly traded company, has disclosed this as its own operational TRX treasury wallet, per its own SEC filing dated 2026-02-12; retrieved and content-checked via WebFetch on 2026-09-21 (page text confirms the tronscan.org link to this exact address is present in the exhibit). Does NOT claim the wallet is permanently exclusive to treasury use, does not claim continuous custody beyond the disclosure date, and does not assert anything about counterparties who send to or receive from this address. Useful operational confounder: a corporate treasury wallet with large periodic TRX inflows/outflows (purchases disclosed via subsequent press releases) is exactly the kind of high-value, high-activity pattern a naive anomaly ranker might flag as suspicious purely on volume/concentration; it is not fraud-related and a future ranker should not treat volume alone as a fraud signal for wallets like this. URLs can rot; this record documents a retrieval-date-stamped observation, not a claim that the URL is permanent evidence.

evidence_type: first-party disclosure: the energy-marketplace operator's own blog post, on its own domain, naming this address as belonging to TronBid.com and carrying the TronScan public tag TronBid_Energy_MarketPlace
notes: Pattern: TronBid.com is a peer-to-peer TRON energy/bandwidth resource marketplace; this is its own operational marketplace address (not a customer's energy-rental-recipient wallet -- filed under other_operational_confounder because the page does not specify whether this address sends, receives, or both, for resource-delegation vs. payment flows). Scope: narrowly supports only that TronBid.com's own blog names this address as belonging to TronBid.com's energy marketplace, as of the page's stated publish/update dates; retrieved and content-checked via WebFetch on 2026-09-21. Does not claim exclusive/permanent control, does not describe the exact transaction role, and does not assert anything about any counterparty. Useful operational confounder: a resource-marketplace's own address is expected to show high fan-out/fan-in transaction counts and many distinct counterparties as an ordinary feature of operating a two-sided marketplace -- exactly the shape a naive anomaly ranker might otherwise flag; documented here without asserting or tuning any anomaly score.
